svg.desc: Logical architecture. Component family colours, explicit boundaries, and consumer-to-provider arrows with source evidence.

g.text: Arrows point from consumer to provider. Colour identifies the consumer family; changed links use green / red.

g.text: runs emulator in isolated worker processes
fetches and executes via mapped memory
creates a mapper through the factory and routes its windows
references console for renderer and input tests
inspects both ROM windows and RAM bank selection
writes PCM through injected output contract
Responsibility overview: representative source files, not an exhaustive class or call graph. Unchanged device routing is summarized.
Consumer -> provider arrows distinguish project references, source inclusion, composition, runtime calls and snapshot consumption.
Each machine owns its CPU registers, flags and memory references; experiment workers retain processes as a host policy. Rendering reconstructs snapshots, not a cycle-accurate pixel pipeline.
Standard MBC1 only; MBC1M wiring, persistent battery saves and MBC3 RTC remain outside this implementation.

Mapper selection, mapped windows and cartridge snapshots use the shared CartridgeMapper / CartridgeMapperState contracts; MBC1 and MBC3 own their banking rules. Debugger inspection reads mapper capabilities
Emulator overview updated for the Windows player and Win32 audio extraction; compiler/toolchain components remain outside this diagram. Windows playback and read-only inspection share one UI thread;
inspector refresh is capped at 4 Hz.

Console and Windows playback share EmulationHost pacing, immutable frame publication, audio lifetime and inspection. Debugger stepping/rewind use the shared debugging service; rich debugger views still

Hosting calls IAudioOutput supplied by the UI; the hosting-to-audio arrow is runtime dispatch only. Only the Win32 adapter references Hosting at compile time. Other audio adapters may implement the same

The console defaults to the bundled SPRITE.GB demo and accepts explicit ROM paths; private ROMs are not automatically copied by its project. This is configuration behavior within the existing front-end
